sections.section_title: Vision, Mission, Goals and Business Strategies

claims.claim_text: The Company is committed to sustainable development, with a balance of economic, environmental, and social dimensions, in order to become a truly sustainable and leading company at the national level.

BEM has established a strategic plan, which allows the Company efficiently manage material sustainability topics that were evaluated on their impacts both inside-out and outside-in perspectives under the principle of Double Materiality.

In 2024, the Company focused on the economic dimension by promoting business competitiveness and good corporate governance, emphasizing its core mission of maintaining service quality to ensure our service users reach their destinations safely.

The Company had a commitment to conserving resources and reducing energy use to mitigate climate change impacts, by continually collaborating both internal and external of the organization such as the collaboration with the Thailand Carbon Neutrality Network (TCNN), which the Company joined in 2022, in order to drive towards the Company’s climate goals and the national targets to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2065.

The Company had also set greenhouse gas reduction targets based on the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and implemented several projects, such as the Solar Power System Installations at Depot (Solar Farm), at Main Workshop Building (Solar Rooftop), and on car park rooftops (Solar Car Park).

As a result of our continuous business operations on sustainability, BEM has been included in the Thailand Sustainability Investment list for the eighth consecutive year with the highest level of “AAA” rating in 2024.

The Company was also ranked on the 2024 list of “ESG100” securities group in the transportation and logistics sector with exceptional performance in the areas of Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG).

In 2024, the Company received several awards, including Transport Deal of the Year award from a global platform, a plaque of honor for being a Climate Action Leading Organization (CALO), the Green Office award at an excellent level, the Employee Experience Awards 2024, the 12th Thailand Social Awards, and Thailand’s Top Corporate Brand Hall of Fame 2024 as a company with the highest corporate brand value for 5 consecutive years in the transportation and logistics sector.
The Company has obtained the opportunity to operate the MRT Orange Line Project (Bang Khun Non - Min Buri (Suwinthawong) Section), which will help reduce greenhouse gas emissions in long-term.

The Company is committed to conducting businesses: Providing services of the expressway and metro systems with safety, convenience, rapidity, reliability, punctuality, and efficiency, in order to improve the quality of people’s lives;

The Company is committed to conducting businesses: Improving the quality and efficiency of the modern and full-service transportation network in order to alleviate traffic problems, preserve the environment, and improve society and the country;

The Company is committed to conducting businesses: Adhering to sustainability principles in business operations by realizing good corporate governance as well as striving for social and environmental responsibility.

To invest in the transportation system projects, expressway and connecting road projects, metro system projects, and related projects under the government policy for the public–private partnership (PPP) in respect of infrastructure, including related businesses, such as various commercial development, taking into consideration of the projects which are beneficial to society and the country, with reasonable business yields;
To build relationships with stakeholders through the corporate social responsibility (CSR) process and communicate to gain an acknowledgment from personnel and people outside the organization;

Bangkok Expressway and Metro Public Company Limited, the leading provider of the expressway and mass rapid transit rail system services, is committed to developing a fully-integrated transportation system to facilitate journeys, alleviate traffic problems in Bangkok and surrounding areas, and upgrade travel to improve the quality of life of people in society.

BEM and Northern Bangkok Expressway Company Limited (“NECL”), a subsidiary of BEM, have obtained concessions from the Expressway Authority of Thailand (EXAT) for the construction and management of three expressways, namely the Si Rat Expressway, the Prachim Ratthaya Expressway, and the Udon Ratthaya Expressway.
The Si Rat Expressway (Second Stage Expressway) is the first large-scale construction project in Thailand on the basis of a public-private partnership with a BTO (Build Transfer Operate) basis.
BEM is exclusively entitled to receive toll revenues throughout the concession period.

BEM is committed to enhancing the quality, efficiency, and sustainability of Thailand’s transportation system while improving the people’s quality of life by delivering convenient, safe, stable, and reliable transportation services.
The Company emphasizes the utilization of materials and technologies with low environmental impact, while focusing on minimizing disturbance to local communities during the construction process.

Operations highlight the importance of enhancing safety performance and environmental responsibility in various related processes, such as regulating and maintaining the Company’s operations in compliance with environmental and safety standards set by regulatory authorities and the public sector.
BEM promotes public transportation for people living in neighboring areas and supports ESG initiatives that create shared value within and beyond the organization.
Plan and define career paths for employees with career, skill and knowledge development, enabling them to grow and progress in the Company according to established goals
Provide mental health benefits, loan and housing benefits, and medical expense discounts for employees and their families, as recommended by the welfare committee

Provide a First Aid room with doctors, nurses, medicines, and medical supplies, along with refill points for medications and supplies that facilitate all employees, including in the bags of train operators
Provide flu vaccinations for four strains and cancer screening benefits for cervical, breast, and prostate cancer
Establish a central unit to conduct additional drinking water quality checks beyond the regular maintenance cycle, ensuring annual testing in all areas
Provide financial assistance to employees affected by natural disasters and human-induced disasters, including floods, fires, storms, landslides, earthquakes, and tsunamis
Conduct training sessions to enhance suppliers’ knowledge of sustainable business practices
Develop a Supplier Code of Conduct and notify supplier to acknowledge and adopt it as a guideline for conducting business with the Company
Prepare contracts fairly and equitable for all suppliers
Ensure timely payment for goods and services (within 30–45 days after receiving the invoice or as contractually agreed)
Develop and share educational materials with suppliers to raise awareness and promote ESG-related initiatives
Evaluate the ESG performance of direct business suppliers (Tier 1 Suppliers) through self-assessments and conduct onsite audits for Significant Tier 1 Suppliers
BEM conducted a materiality assessment of topics associated with business operations in line with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) 2021 Standards to identify and report key ESG topics.

Acting in compliance with the GRI Standards, the Company is assured that the materiality assessment and reporting are reliable, transparent, and comparable with other organizations in the same industry.
The Company will review the material sustainability topics every three years.
BEM has adjusted the Company’s criteria for considering impact significance by employing a matrix to assess impact severity and tendency.
BEM was able to identify a total of 14 material sustainability topics, covering environmental, social, and economic & governance aspects.
BEM places importance on governing IT security and Data privacy to support its internal operations.
The Company has made improvements to ensure that the IT system is secure and consistent with the ISO/IEC 27001 international standard.
The Company has implemented practices for the protection of stakeholders’ personal data in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019).

BEM has plans to expand its services through digital platforms and has invested in enhancing the efficiency of its system infrastructure in order to accommodate the growth of system usage in the future.
The Company has also developed a Cyber Attack Response Plan to enhance information technology security and protection on the privacy of stakeholders against personal data breaches.

BEM aims to prevent information technology security breaches, ensure no impact on customers, employees or other stakeholders, and maintain a record of zero confirmed personal data breach complaints from customers, external organizations, or government agencies.
In 2024, BEM detected two cyberattacks, which were successfully contained without affecting services or compromising personal data.

No customers, employees or other stakeholders were impacted, and no confirmed personal data breach complaints were reported by customers, external organizations, or government agencies, aligning with the Company’s target.

BEM has announced an Information Security Policy and developed an Information Technology Security Manual as a guideline for employees, system administrators, and external parties working with the Company.
BEM has appointed an Information Security Management Committee to oversee and manage information technology security.

In 2024, BEM expanded its ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification to cover the Expressway Toll Collection System, the Intelligent Traffic Control System, and Back Office’s IT Infrastructure for both the Expressway and Rail businesses.

BEM is committed to developing a supply chain and procurement process that addresses sustainability risk issues, such as environmental impact, occupational health and safety, human rights breaches, business ethics breaches, anti-corruption, and bribery.

The Company has established a policy and strategies for supply chain management, and implemented the Supplier Code of Conduct as a standard framework for all suppliers, as well as continuously enhanced procurement and supply chain management processes to align with sustainable development principles.
BEM has set a target for all new suppliers to pass sustainability screening criteria, which covers environmental aspect, social, human rights and labor aspect, and business ethics aspect.
The Company aims for a target supplier satisfaction rate of no less than 85%.
In 2024, all new suppliers successfully met the set criteria at 100%, while the supplier satisfaction rate reached 99.11%, which is in line with the set target.
New suppliers acknowledge and comply with the Supplier Code of Conduct: 2024 Performance = 100%; Short-Term Target (2024) = 100%; Long-Term Target (2030) = 100%.
New suppliers passed sustainability screening criteria: 2024 Performance = 100%; Short-Term Target (2024) = 100%; Long-Term Target (2030) = 100%.
Significant Tier-1 Suppliers assessed on sustainability through self-assessment: 2024 Performance = 100%; Short-Term Target (2024) = 100%; Long-Term Target (2030) = 100%.
Tier-1 Suppliers assessed on sustainability through self-assessment: 2024 Performance = 85.06%; Short-Term Target (2024) = 75%; Long-Term Target (2030) = 100%.
Supplier payment period: 2024 Performance = 37 days; Short-Term Target (2024) = 30–45 days; Long-Term Target (2030) = 30–45 days.
Supplier satisfaction: 2024 Performance = 99.11%; Short-Term Target (2024) = ≥85%; Long-Term Target (2030) = ≥90%.

BEM has established targets and performance indicators for its innovation development, such as the Adaptive Traffic Signage Control Board project, which aims to reduce equipment investment costs by 30%, and the Asset Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics (ACMD) project for various systems including signaling system, track work system, and water system, with a target of achieving 100% project development success.

In 2024, the Adaptive Traffic Signage Control Board project successfully achieved a 77% reduction in equipment investment costs, meeting the target, while the Asset Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics (ACMD) project achieved 95% success, slightly below the target due to the ongoing development of technology for operational inspections and monitoring on equipment of signaling system, which is expected to be completed within the first quarter of 2025.
BEM has established the Innovation policy to promote innovation in business operations grounded in a strong commitment to social and environmental responsibility.
In 2024, BEM invested in research, development, and implementation of innovations across eleven projects with a total investment value of over 6.86 million THB.

Development of new technological innovations by BEM includes three major projects: the Adaptive Traffic Signage Control Board Project, the Asset Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics (ACMD) project, which has been developed and is ready for use, and the development of equipment for inspection of wire strands in Expressway structure, a project that has been under study and continuous development since 2022.
Implementation of innovation to improve and enhance service delivery efficiency and effectiveness includes eight projects with a total investment value exceeding 6.86 million THB.

BEM found that the development and implementation of these innovations contribute to savings in both investment and operational costs, while also enhancing work processes, service delivery efficiency and effectiveness.
To select electronic parts according to ROHS standards, which release chemicals at a rate that does not impact the environment.
BEM has set a customer satisfaction’s target at least 92%.
In 2024, BEM conducted a customer satisfaction survey with 2,884 respondents, achieving a satisfied level of 95.98%.
The complaint rate was 0.01 cases per 100,000 trips for the expressway business and 0.02 cases per 100,000 passengers for the rail business, both meeting the set targets.
BEM has set targets for the Easy Pass Availability on the expressway system at no less than 99.90%.
The Company also aims for at least 96% of to be responded to within 12 minutes (Rescue Incident Response within 12 Minutes).

For the rail business, the targets for the MRT Blue Line are as follows: Train Service Availability (TSA) and Train Service Punctuality (TSP) at no less than 99.20%, and Train Availability (TA) at no less than 99.70%.
For the MRT Purple Line, the targets are Train Service Availability (TSA) and Train Service Punctuality (TSP) at no less than 99.25%, and Train Availability (TA) at no less than 99.75%.
In 2024, BEM’s overall performance either met or exceeded the established targets.
Easy Pass Availability reached 99.95%, and Rescue Incident Response within 12 Minutes met the target at 96%.
For the MRT Blue Line, Train Service Punctuality (TSP) was recorded at 99.64% and Train Availability (TA) at 100%.
The MRT Purple Line achieved 100% for both Train Service Availability (TSA) and Train Availability (TA), while Train Service Punctuality (TSP) reached 99.99%.

BEM continuously manages customer relationships in alignment with its corporate strategy, setting a target satisfaction score of at least 95% for the rail business, at least 90% for the expressway business, and at least 90% for the commercial development business.

BEM is committed to operating business in accordance with the principles of sustainability, good corporate governance, as well as social and environmental responsibility, and strict adherence to code of conduct.
The Company regularly reviews its policies to ensure they are appropriate and aligned with laws and international standards.
Furthermore, the Company consistently evaluates and reports its performances according to these policies to create long-term economic value and fairness to all stakeholders across the value chain.
Focus on zero-tolerance policy towards corruption and bribery.
Annual mandatory communication and training on corporate governance and code of conduct for directors and employees.
No incidents of corruption or bribery within BEM.
100% of directors and employees received communication and training on corporate governance and business ethics.
BEM operates in accordance with its good Corporate Governance Policy to ensure an efficient, transparent, and accountable management system.
The Corporate Governance Policy is reviewed on an annual basis.
BEM has established the Corporate Governance, Risk Management and Sustainable Development Committee to assess the adequacy and suitability of policies at the strategic level.
BEM requires the election of new Board Directors to replace those who are retired by rotation, following transparent and fair criteria and procedures for the nomination and appointment of directors.
Integrating sustainability risk criteria covering Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) dimensions into the continuous organizational risk assessment process.
Risk management training was provided for a total of 48 executives and employees.
The Company has established a Risk Management Policy and an Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework according to COSO standards as part of its business planning.

The Company prepares an annual risk management plan and a risk management manual to ensure that risk management processes are implemented systematically, aligned with business strategies and acceptable risk levels, and are responsive to rapidly changing global trends.

The Board of Directors has delegated the Corporate Governance, Risk Management, and Sustainable Development Committee, which is structurally independent from the Company’s business lines, to oversee and approve the Company’s risk management policy and frameworks.
The Company reports enterprise risks to the Corporate Governance, Risk Management, and Sustainable Development Committee and/or the Board of Directors on a quarterly basis.
A comprehensive risk assessment for the year 2024 has been conducted.
Establish and regularly update the Company’s information security policy to ensure alignment with current legal and regulatory requirements
Implement systems to prevent and control unauthorized access to information systems
Identify, assess, and manage information technology (IT) security risks associated with the Company’s services
Conduct system recovery drills or simulations at least once a year to ensure readiness in the event of disruptions to key services or financial data

Continuously audit, monitor, and improve information security processes in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001, applying this standard to critical systems. External audits are conducted to assess internal controls over IT systems
Promote awareness through internal communication, employee training, and ongoing capacity building related to cybersecurity and data protection
Enhance service delivery processes, systems, and equipment to ensure continued efficiency, convenience, and safety under all conditions
Strengthen the Company’s logistics and access systems to improve operational reach in flooded affected areas
Establish alternative approaches for the management of goods and spare parts inventory to support timely maintenance operations

For new transportation infrastructure under concession agreements, ensure that the design of structural elements and protective systems addresses flood risks. This includes designing entrances/exits above historical flood levels and installing flood barriers (e.g., flood boards or stop logs) and flood doors at underground station access points to prevent water intrusion. These protective systems have already been implemented in current projects such as the MRT Blue Line and MRT Purple Line.

Develop efficient and environmentally friendly systems, equipment, and service processes across the value chain in compliance with government regulations to support organizational efforts in reducing greenhouse gas emissions
Implement organizational greenhouse gas reduction initiatives

Closely monitor the enforcement and development of climate change-related laws, both existing and upcoming. Summarize key legal requirements and communicate them directly to the responsible departments to ensure timely and effective compliance.
The Company has set targets to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and net zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 2065.
These targets align with the national GHG emissions reduction roadmap to mitigate the impacts of climate change.
The Company implements action plans with resource management guidelines, such as energy usage, pollution control, and efficient waste management.
The Company has established an Energy Management Committee, which is responsible for planning and managing energy reduction within the organization.

BEM is committed to aligning with the Paris Agreement and the 26th session of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of the Parties (UNFCCC COP26), which aims to limit an increase in the global temperature to 1.5°C.
BEM has established a Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) process to set the science-based GHG emissions reduction targets.
The short-term target for 2024 is a 4% reduction, representing a reduction of 138,081 tons CO₂e, while the long-term target for 2030 is a 28% reduction (4% per year).
BEM conducted a verification of the corporate GHG emissions across all three scopes, with organizational boundaries for calculation and reporting covering 99% of operations.
Overall, BEM reduced GHG emissions by 1.59%, achieving a 49.76% reduction in Scope 1 GHG emissions that met the set target.
Energy consumption increased by 2.53% in 2024, not meeting the set targets.
BEM has planned to replace 24 internal combustion engine vehicles with electric vehicles by 2030.

In 2024, the Company added seven more electric vehicles, bringing the total to nine, resulting in a fuel reduction of 7,396 liters, a decrease in energy cost by approximately 243,997 THB and a reduction in GHG emissions of 20.27 tons CO₂e.

It is estimated that once all 24 cars have been replaced with electric vehicles, fossil fuel consumption will decrease by 50,646 liters per year, reducing energy costs by approximately 1.58 million THB per year and GHG emissions by 140 tons CO₂e per year.

In 2024, BEM replaced 12 executive internal combustion engine vehicles with electric vehicles, resulting in a fuel reduction of 25,183.44 liters, energy cost savings of approximately 831,000 THB, and a reduction of 69 tons CO₂e of GHG emissions.

In 2024, BEM planned to replace 818 high-pressure sodium (HPS) streetlights with Light Emitting Diode (LED) lights, aiming to save approximately 1.46 million THB in energy costs per year, reduce energy consumption by 357,126 kWh per year, and decrease GHG emissions by 178 tons CO₂e per year.

The installation was fully completed in October 2024, resulting in actual savings of approximately 349,000 THB, a reduction in energy consumption of 122,895 kWh, and a decrease in GHG emissions by 61.32 tons CO₂e.

BEM implemented a project to improve air conditioning efficiency in the ventilation shaft buildings by replacing 20 units of conventional, or fixed-speed, air conditioning system with inverter sets in eight ventilation shafts of the MRT Blue Line Project.

This initiative is expected to save approximately 2.69 million THB in energy costs per year and reduce energy consumption by 653,805 kWh per year, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 327 tons CO₂e per year.

The installation was fully completed in November 2024, resulting in actual savings of approximately 447,000 THB and a reduction in energy consumption of 108,967.50 kWh, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 54.47 tons CO₂e.

BEM relocated 54 units of compressors to positions with better heat dissipation along with installed ventilation fans to alternate operation between fans and air conditioning systems at specified intervals, within stations in the MRT Purple Line Project.

This initiative is expected to save approximately 1.97 million THB in energy costs per year and reduce energy consumption by 478,515 kWh per year, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 239 tons CO₂e per year.

The equipment replacement and installation were fully completed in December 2024, resulting in actual savings of approximately 164,000 THB and a reduction in energy consumption of 39,876.25 kWh, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 19.93 tons CO₂e.

BEM upgraded the Fresh Air Control System from manual to automatic operations by integrating software for motorized dampers in order to work automatically based on predefined functions and conditions at nine stations of the MRT Blue Line.

This initiative is expected to save approximately 1.05 million THB in energy costs per year and reduce energy consumption by 254,735 kWh per year, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 127 tons CO₂e per year.

The equipment replacement and installation were fully completed in October 2024, resulting in actual savings of approximately 261,000 THB and a reduction in energy consumption of 63,683.76 kWh, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 31.84 tons CO₂e.
BEM has installed air curtains at entrances and exits of five stations within the MRT Blue Line Project, totaling 41 locations.

This initiative is expected to save approximately 4.21 million THB in energy costs per year and reduce energy consumption by 1,022,365 kWh per year, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 511 tons CO₂e per year.

The equipment replacement and installation were fully completed in December 2024, resulting in actual savings of approximately 349,000 THB and a reduction in energy consumption of 85,197.08 kWh, equating to a GHG emissions reduction of 42.59 tons CO₂e.
BEM is committed to conducting business with a strong emphasis on occupational health and safety, ensuring the well-being of all stakeholders.

This commitment includes building trust and customer satisfaction through effective safety measures, consistent inspections and maintenances of infrastructures, and adherence to a certified occupational health and safety management system in compliance with ISO 45001 standards.

BEM has set a target of zero fatalities for customers, employees, and contractors, along with a Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) target of zero cases per 1 million hours worked for employees and contractors.
In 2024, BEM recorded no fatalities among customers and employees; however, there was one contractor fatality due to a work-related accident.
The LTIFR for employees and contractors were 0.62 and 0.96 cases per 1 million hours worked, respectively, exceeding the target.

BEM has established health and safety policy and practices, along with an occupational health and safety management system that applies to employees, contractors, and suppliers operating within the Company’s premises.
The policy and management systems comply with the Occupational Safety, Health and Work Environment Act B.E. 2554 (A.D. 2011).
Additionally, the rail business’s occupational health and safety management system is ISO 45001 certified, and the Company plans to extend ISO 45001 certification to the expressway business by 2026.
BEM has obtained ISO 45001 certification for the rail business’s occupational health and safety management system during 2024–2025, covering 48.81% of its operations.

BEM sets a target of at least 85% employee participation in the engagement and happiness survey, an employee engagement and happiness score target of no less than 75% and an average target of 40 training hours per employee per year.
In 2024, 93.70% of employees participated in the engagement and happiness survey, exceeding the target.
The employee engagement and happiness score reached 80.80% and an average of 41.40 training hours per employee per year, also surpassing the set target.
BEM has established personnel development policy and practices as guidelines for recruiting, developing, and retaining employees.
BEM has implemented the Human Capital Development Framework, which covers six aspects, as the basis for continuous operations.
In 2024, BEM reviewed and defined the Human Resource Management Strategy 2024-2028 to empower the Company’s current and future competitiveness.

BEM is committed to ensuring a high quality of life for employees, fostering a positive work environment and providing comprehensive benefits that uphold human rights and labor rights, exceeding legal requirements to maintain competitiveness within the industry.
Employee benefits include bonuses, life and accident insurance, a provident fund, medical benefits, annual health check-ups, and well-being promotions regarding both physical and mental health.

These supports include telemedicine services, the “BEM Burn Your Fat Get Your Health Season 8” wellness campaign, fitness rooms, and medical rooms at all work locations, where employees can receive treatment and health consultations.

Recognizing the importance of mental well-being, the Company also provides online mental health consultations with psychologists, ensuring employees have access to professional support whenever needed.
BEM has established a Welfare Committee elected by employees, and encourages the formation of various clubs to promote sports, recreation, and overall employee well-being.
BEM conducts employee performance appraisals once a year based on a 90-degree evaluation from direct supervisors.

The Company has implemented a Performance Management System (PMS), Team-based performance appraisal, and agile conversations to manage personnel performance and achieve good operating results continually.

The appraisal criteria consists of key performance indicators (KPIs) that rely on the SMART principle in defining indicator targets, core competency, managerial competency, and functional competency, incorporating S A C T L as a measurement criterion.

Apart from being used to analyze and define training programs according to the “Academy Framework”, the results of employee performance appraisals are also utilized to determine remuneration, such as salary increased and annual bonuses.
BEM has prepared an Individual Development Plan for employees whose performance has been evaluated as “unacceptable, below standard, or needing improvement”.

BEM is committed to retaining talented employees and attracting high-potential candidates to support business growth, which is a crucial factor in maintaining a competitive advantage and enabling the organization to achieve its targets.

In 2024, the Company welcomed 28 interns for practical training and launched the “BEM NEW HORIZON” project, an initiative designed to introduce young individuals to the real working environment of MRT Blue Line station staff and provide future educational and career opportunities.
In support of diversity and inclusion, the Company actively promotes the employment of people with disabilities, ensuring they have job opportunities, career stability, and sustainable income.

In 2024, the Company employed 38 people with disabilities through partnerships with organizations such as the Autism Thai Foundation, the Sharing Club for Intellectually Disabled Children, the Federation of Disabled Workers of Thailand, and the Bangkok Employment Office Area 10.
In 2024, 39 employees were transferred or appointed through internal recruitment, accounting for 0.94% of vacant positions filled by internal candidates.
In 2024, a total of 279 employees were promoted, comprising 141 male employees and 138 female employees, representing a promotion ratio of 50.5% male to 49.5% female.

BEM is committed to ensuring a high quality of life for employees, fostering a positive work environment and providing comprehensive benefits that uphold human rights and labor rights, exceeding legal requirements to maintain competitiveness within the industry.

claims.claim_text: BEM operates under Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Policy, and Environmental and Climate Policy.
The Company is committed to reducing impacts and concerns while fostering opportunities for communities to genuinely participate in their own development.
BEM sets a target of community satisfaction on community relations promotion activities at not less than 98%.
The number of complaints from communities along expressway routes is targeted at not over 0.10 cases per 100,000 trips.
The number of complaints from communities along MRT routes and Depots is targeted at not over 0.10 cases per 100,000 passengers.
The Company aims to engage at least 20 communities in CSR projects and has set a target for zero complaints from society and communities.
In 2024, community satisfaction on community relations promotion activities was 95.83%.
The number of complaints from communities along expressway routes was 0.0041 cases per 100,000 trips.
The number of complaints from communities along MRT routes and Depots was 0.0039 cases per 100,000 passengers.
A total of 173 communities participated in BEM’s CSR projects.
There were 23 community complaints in total, of which 19 cases were related to the Company’s operations and have been 100% resolved.
BEM has announced its Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Policy as a guideline for all employees to implement and integrate into every work process.
BEM has established a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) strategy focused on improving quality of life and well-being, with an emphasis on safety, climate responsibility, and environmental care.

BEM emphasizes social responsibility and community relations operations under the CSR Roadmap, ensuring stakeholder engagement, respect for diversity, equality, and inclusion, and promoting collaboration with all partners.
The 'HAPPY JOURNEY' initiative aims to promote good health and safe living through quality and safety in service provision, as well as community and public health projects.
BEM CARE 2024 Project: 'Say Goodbye to Office Syndrome'

Reducing environmental impacts and climate change through innovation and technology for the environment, clean energy, and efficient waste management with the target to support the achievement of the national Carbon Neutrality Target in 2050.

In 2024, BEM organized a total of 27 CSR activities with a budget of over 23.34 million THB to promote and strengthen relationships with society and communities under the Happiness Promotion strategy.
BEM is committed to developing and driving its business in parallel with sustainability, operating under the principles of good corporate governance, social and environmental responsibility.

BEM, in collaboration with the Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA), organized a tree planting event as part of the Ministry of Transport (MOT) Project for Tree Planting in Honor of His Majesty the King.
A total of 50 executives and employees participated in planting 440 trees as part of efforts to conserve the environment.

BEM, in collaboration with CH. Karnchang Public Company Limited, Bangkok Metro Networks Limited, and government agencies such as the Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) and the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT), launched the 6th art exhibition under the theme “INTO THE SEA - Dive Deep to Discover a New World.”
The exhibition showcases the beauty and mystery of the underwater world, aiming to raise awareness about ocean threats and inspire visitors to appreciate, protect, and conserve marine resources.

The “A Good Deed A Day” campaign encourages visitors to collect stamps for every 200 THB spent on purchases or services at Metro Mall, MRT Phahon Yothin Station. Each stamp includes a CSR kit. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to the Endangered Coral Nursery Research Project under the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources.
The company achieved high media engagement (over 2.5 million times) and reached nearly 96,000 participants.

BEM conducts the stakeholder identification process by taking into account stakeholders who are both positively and negatively affected by the Company’s operations. This is in line with the operating principles of AA1000 Stakeholder Engagement Standard (AA1000SES).

BEM implements a risk management process for each stakeholder group, in accordance with international principles and standards by defining preventive guidelines, operational framework, and resource allocation to effectively mitigate impacts that may occur to each stakeholder group.

BEM has established the criteria for analyzing and prioritizing stakeholders, namely the level of interest in stakeholder engagement and the level of impact from the Company’s operations on the stakeholders.

BEM believes that employees are valuable resources and key stakeholders who help drive the organization forward towards sustainable growth. Therefore, the Company encourages employees to actively participate in proposing sustainability-related initiatives through a strong corporate culture.

BEM has assigned the Sustainability Development Department, which reports directly to the Deputy Managing Director for Business Development and Expressway Operations, to be responsible for issues relating to stakeholder engagement.
Stakeholder engagement can take various approaches, including informal discussions, meetings, seminars, evaluation surveys, and questionnaires.
BEM places importance on planning engagement with stakeholders related to the Company’s business value chain and sustainability issues.

BEM is committed to delivering high-quality services to all service user groups equally, ensuring fairness for individuals, including the general public and those requiring assistance such as children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.

The Company prioritizes the design of appropriate infrastructure and service facilities, in line with the Universal Design principles, to ensure seamless accessibility at stations and on trains for all users.

BEM listens to feedback and complaints related to services, convenience, and other concerns from all user groups. This input is used to improve facilities and services, ensuring the Company can deliver quality and equitable services for all users.

BEM has established guidelines for supporting community and social activities by identifying target communities that are or may be affected by its operations, such as communities near the depot and those neighboring expressway and rail routes.

To address community needs, expectations, and potential impacts, BEM has implemented a survey process for these aspects through field engagement in order to assess community and social concerns that may be negatively affected by the Company’s operations.
In 2024, the Company received 23 human rights complaints from communities, which were analyzed and categorized.
BEM has established dedicated channels for human rights complaints and stakeholder suggestions related to human rights issues.
BEM is committed to protecting human rights by ensuring fair treatment for employees and all stakeholders.

BEM actively promotes awareness and consideration for special-needs passengers, including the elderly, people with disabilities, pregnant women, and individuals with strollers, through the “Priority Lift” project.
